topics.label: Continuous Integration
topics.desc: The practice of merging code to a shared branch frequently and running automated builds and tests on every push, catching integration failures early via tools like GitHub Actions.

topics.label: Delivery vs Deployment
topics.desc: Continuous delivery keeps every change releasable behind a manual approval gate across dev, staging, and prod, while continuous deployment ships every passing commit automatically.

topics.label: CI/CD Pipeline
topics.desc: An automated sequence of stages and jobs triggered by commits or pull requests that builds, tests, and ships software, defined in YAML for runners like those of CircleCI to execute.

topics.label: Build, Test, Deploy Stages
topics.desc: The canonical pipeline phases run in order with gates: compile and bundle into versioned artifacts, run unit and integration tests and linters, then promote the result to an environment.

topics.label: Deployment Strategies
topics.desc: Techniques to ship with minimal risk and downtime, including blue-green swapping two environments, canary releasing to a small subset, and rolling updates batch by batch.

topics.label: GitHub Actions
topics.desc: GitHub's built-in CI/CD platform that runs YAML-defined workflows on hosted or self-hosted runners, triggered by repository events and composed from reusable marketplace actions.

topics.label: GitLab CI & Jenkins
topics.desc: Other major pipeline engines: GitLab's integrated .gitlab-ci.yml runners, and Jenkins, the veteran self-hosted automation server with scriptable Jenkinsfiles and a vast plugin ecosystem.

topics.label: Docker
topics.desc: The dominant platform for building and running containers, packaging an app with its dependencies into a portable image that runs identically on any host with a container runtime.

topics.label: Containers vs VMs
topics.desc: Containers share the host OS kernel for lightweight, fast-starting process isolation, whereas virtual machines virtualize hardware and run a full guest OS, trading speed for stronger isolation.

topics.label: Container Images
topics.desc: Immutable, layered, tagged filesystem snapshots bundling an app and its runtime, built from a base image and instantiated as running containers across any compatible host.

topics.label: Dockerfile
topics.desc: A declarative text recipe of instructions like FROM, COPY, RUN, and CMD that the Docker engine executes step by step to assemble a reproducible container image.

topics.label: Layers & Multi-Stage Builds
topics.desc: Each Dockerfile instruction is a cached layer, so ordering steps by volatility speeds rebuilds, while multi-stage builds compile in a heavy image then copy artifacts into a slim one.

topics.label: Docker Compose
topics.desc: A tool that defines and runs multi-container applications from a single YAML file, wiring services, networks, and volumes together for local development and simple deployments.

topics.label: Container Registries
topics.desc: Repositories that store and distribute tagged container images, such as Docker Hub, GitHub Container Registry (GHCR), and cloud registries like Amazon ECR for CI/CD to pull and push.

topics.label: Container Orchestration
topics.desc: Automating the deployment, scheduling, networking, scaling, and self-healing of many containers across a cluster of machines, the problem Kubernetes and Docker Swarm solve.

topics.label: Kubernetes
topics.desc: The de facto container orchestrator that runs declarative workloads across a cluster, reconciling desired state through a control plane and scheduling containers onto worker nodes.

topics.label: Pods
topics.desc: Kubernetes' smallest deployable unit: one or more tightly coupled containers sharing a network namespace and storage, scheduled together and treated as a single ephemeral instance.

topics.label: Deployments & Probes
topics.desc: Controllers that keep a desired number of pod replicas running and roll out new versions gradually, using liveness and readiness probes to restart or hold traffic from unhealthy pods.

topics.label: Services & Ingress
topics.desc: Kubernetes networking: Services give a stable virtual IP and DNS to a changing set of pods, while Ingress routes external HTTP/HTTPS traffic to them by host and path with TLS.

topics.label: Autoscaling
topics.desc: Automatically adjusting capacity to match load, scaling pod replicas horizontally on CPU or custom metrics, adjusting resource limits vertically, or adding cluster nodes on demand.

topics.label: Managed Kubernetes
topics.desc: Cloud-operated Kubernetes control planes like Amazon EKS, Google GKE, and Azure AKS that remove the burden of running masters, etcd, and upgrades yourself.

topics.label: Platform as a Service
topics.desc: A hosting model where the provider manages servers, runtime, and scaling so you just push code or a container, trading fine-grained control for speed and low operational overhead.

topics.label: Vercel
topics.desc: A frontend cloud optimized for Next.js and static sites, offering Git-driven deploys, instant preview URLs per pull request, edge functions, and a global CDN out of the box.

topics.label: Netlify
topics.desc: A platform for static sites and Jamstack apps with Git-based continuous deployment, deploy previews, serverless functions, forms, and edge handlers on a built-in CDN.

topics.label: Heroku, Render & Fly
topics.desc: General-purpose PaaS options deploying services, databases, and containers from a repo or Dockerfile: Heroku pioneered the model, Render and Railway modernized it, and Fly.io runs near users.

topics.label: VPS Hosting
topics.desc: A rented virtual private server with root access and a full Linux OS, from providers like DigitalOcean, Linode, or Hetzner, giving control at the cost of self-managing everything.

topics.label: Static Hosting
topics.desc: Serving prebuilt HTML, CSS, and JS files directly from a CDN or object storage with no server runtime, via GitHub Pages, Cloudflare Pages, or Amazon S3 plus CloudFront.

topics.label: Choosing a Host
topics.desc: Weighing control, cost, scaling, region coverage, and operational effort to pick between static hosting, PaaS, a VPS, serverless, or full cloud for a given workload.

topics.label: Cloud Providers
topics.desc: The hyperscalers offering on-demand infrastructure and managed services over the internet, led by Amazon Web Services (AWS), Google Cloud Platform, and Microsoft Azure.

topics.label: Cloud Compute
topics.desc: Rentable virtual machines and instance types that form the elastic backbone of the cloud, such as AWS EC2, Google Compute Engine, and Azure Virtual Machines.

topics.label: Object Storage
topics.desc: Massively scalable, durable storage for files and blobs accessed over HTTP, like AWS S3, Google Cloud Storage, and Azure Blob, the standard home for assets and backups.

topics.label: Managed Databases
topics.desc: Provider-operated database services that handle backups, patching, replication, and failover, such as AWS RDS, Aurora, and DynamoDB, removing most database administration toil.

topics.label: Regions & Zones
topics.desc: Geographic regions each containing multiple isolated availability zones, the foundation for placing resources near users and architecting for fault tolerance and low latency.

topics.label: Identity & Access (IAM)
topics.desc: The cloud permission system of users, roles, and policies enforcing least-privilege access to resources, with AWS IAM as the canonical model for who can do what.

topics.label: Serverless Functions
topics.desc: Event-driven FaaS code that runs on demand without managing servers, billed per invocation and auto-scaling to zero, exemplified by AWS Lambda and Google Cloud Functions.

topics.label: Edge Functions
topics.desc: Serverless code that runs at CDN points of presence close to users for ultra-low latency, on platforms like Cloudflare Workers, Vercel Edge Functions, and Deno Deploy.

topics.label: Backend as a Service
topics.desc: Ready-made backends bundling database, authentication, storage, and APIs so frontends can ship without custom servers, via Firebase, Supabase, and Appwrite.

topics.label: Firebase
topics.desc: Google's BaaS providing realtime and document databases, authentication, hosting, and cloud functions, popular for quickly building mobile and web app backends.

topics.label: Supabase
topics.desc: An open-source Firebase alternative built on PostgreSQL, offering an instant REST and realtime API, authentication, storage, and edge functions over a relational database.

topics.label: Nginx
topics.desc: A high-performance, event-driven web server, used as a reverse proxy, load balancer, and static file server, that with the older process-based Apache handles most web traffic.

topics.label: Reverse Proxy
topics.desc: A server sitting in front of backend apps that forwards client requests to them, centralizing TLS termination, routing, caching, and load balancing while hiding internal topology.

topics.label: Load Balancers
topics.desc: A component that distributes incoming traffic across multiple server instances for scale and redundancy, using algorithms like round-robin and health checks, at layer 4 or layer 7.

topics.label: SSL/TLS Termination
topics.desc: Decrypting inbound HTTPS at a reverse proxy or load balancer so backends handle plain HTTP, centralizing certificate management and offloading cryptographic work from app servers.

topics.label: Let's Encrypt & Certbot
topics.desc: A free, automated certificate authority and the Certbot client that issue and auto-renew TLS certificates via the ACME protocol, making HTTPS the default for any site.

topics.label: DNS for Deploys
topics.desc: Pointing a domain at your infrastructure using A, AAAA, and CNAME records and managing TTLs and propagation to cut over traffic during deployments without downtime.

topics.label: Ports & Firewalls
topics.desc: Controlling which network ports a host exposes and filtering inbound and outbound traffic with firewalls, security groups, and tools like ufw or iptables to limit attack surface.

topics.label: Infrastructure as Code
topics.desc: Defining and provisioning servers, networks, and cloud resources through version-controlled declarative files instead of manual clicks, making infrastructure reproducible and reviewable.

topics.label: Terraform
topics.desc: HashiCorp's cloud-agnostic IaC tool that uses declarative HCL and a state file to plan and apply provider-managed resources across AWS, GCP, Azure, and many others.

topics.label: Pulumi & CloudFormation
topics.desc: Other IaC tools: Pulumi defines infrastructure in general-purpose languages like TypeScript and Python, while AWS CloudFormation provisions stacks from native JSON or YAML templates.

topics.label: Configuration Management
topics.desc: Automating consistent server setup and software state with agentless tools like Ansible running idempotent YAML playbooks over SSH, plus alternatives like Chef and Puppet.

topics.label: Environment Config
topics.desc: Externalizing settings from code into environment variables and config files per environment, following twelve-factor principles so the same build runs in dev, staging, and prod.

topics.label: Secrets Management
topics.desc: Securely storing and injecting credentials, API keys, and tokens at runtime via vaults and CI/CD secret stores like HashiCorp Vault and GitHub Actions secrets, never in source.

topics.label: Immutable Infrastructure
topics.desc: Replacing servers with freshly built images on every change rather than patching them in place, eliminating configuration drift and making rollbacks a redeploy of a prior image.

topics.label: GitOps
topics.desc: Managing infrastructure and deployments by treating a Git repository as the single source of truth, with agents like Argo CD or Flux continuously reconciling the cluster to it.
